text:
alex: Heads-up - opening a quick TF question. I'm about to change the VPC egress routing for the analytics cluster so NAT failover prefers the new zonal NATs instead of the shared cross-az NAT. Want to make sure the healthcheck + route priority combination is sane.

mira: quick context: currently we use a single route table per private subnet with a default route -> natgw (elastic) in the shared egress AZ. New plan is per-az natgw and update route table routing policy to prefer local nat.

ravi: any reason not to use route table `propagation` + TGW? we want to avoid circular dependencies in TF.

alex: TGW not an option here; this is a regional analytics VPC with strict egress auditing and PrivateLink consumers. Keeping it simple with per-az NATs. main question is about the healthcheck / route swap order to avoid blackholing in the canary rollout.

mira: ok. in TF I was thinking about: 1) create new natgw in each AZ 2) attach EIP 3) add route entries with higher priority (lower numeric weight) for local nat and fallback to shared nat 4) healthcheck monitors that mark the local nat as unhealthy -> change route.

jen: TF note: AWS route tables don't expose explicit numeric priorities. We usually implement priority via separate route tables per AZ and change associations, or use more specific routes by prefix (not applicable). Are you planning to update associations?

alex: good call. Plan A: keep single route table per subnet but replace default route target to the local nat when we can. We want zero-downtime switchover for in-flight connections. Plan B: create a new route table per AZ and re-associate subnets during rollout so change is contained. Thoughts?

ravi: Plan B safer imo. Re-assoc is atomic and lets us rollback by re-associating back. Slightly more TF complexity but less transient state.

mira: agree with Ravi. Also need to wire the healthcheck. Suggest `route53 healthcheck` + `cloudwatch alarm` that triggers a Lambda which updates a `ssm parameter` that the TF can read? that's awkward. Alternatively use BGP-like probe from our egress-canary lambda that marks the NAT's health in a small Dynamo table and an operator job runs the re-association.

alex: I want to avoid manual operator job if possible. Can deploy-bot run an infra action?

deploy-bot: @alex I can run the canary apply job if PR includes the `infra:canary` tag and an approved runbook file. Current status: no matching PR.

jen: For automation we typically avoid TF-driven health re-assoc. TF is declarative and not great for frequent dynamic failovers. Better to have a small controller (lambda or k8s operator) that re-associates the route table when the NAT health flips. TF owns the stable desired state (route tables exist, associations templates), controller flips the association resource via AWS API.

alex: sounds reasonable. So TF will create per-az route tables and the controller will update associations. Controller will watch an SSM param or Dynamo entry updated by healthcheck probes.

mira: TL;DR implementation plan: - TF: create `natgw_local_az` resources, EIPs, per-az `route_table_local` and associate subnets (initially pointing at shared nat, not the local ones) - Health probes (lambda) run in each AZ, write status to Dynamo - Controller (lambda/ecs task) reads Dynamo and re-associates `route_table_local` to point default route at local natgw when healthy; rollback if unhealthy - Deploy canary in one AZ first with `infra:canary` tag and `deploy-bot` runbook.

ravi: we should also add an explicit `depends_on` in TF so NATs and EIPs are created before route tables are populated. And add lifecycle prevent_destroy on the shared eip while in canary.

jen: Also remember to add cloudtrail logs + KMS key perms for controller lambdas. Security needs to review IAM for `ec2:ReplaceRouteTableAssociation` etc.

alex: thanks. I'll draft the PR with TF snippets and the controller lambda skeleton. Posting a snippet here for quick peek:

```hcl
resource "aws_route_table" "rt_local_az" {
  count = length(var.azs)
  vpc_id = var.vpc_id
  tags = { Name = "rt-${var.vpc_name}-${element(var.azs, count.index)}" }
}

resource "aws_route" "default_local" {
  count = length(var.azs)
  route_table_id = aws_route_table.rt_local_az[count.index].id
  destination_cidr_block = "0.0.0.0/0"
  gateway_id = null
  nat_gateway_id = aws_eip_association.eip[count.index].nat_gateway_id # placeholder, controller will update association target
  depends_on = [aws_eip.eip]
}
```

mira: looks fine for skeleton. We should avoid referencing a runtime updated nat id in the static route resource if controller will do the replace; maybe create a placeholder `aws_route` with target to shared nat then controller calls `ReplaceRoute` to point to local natgw.

alex: got it. I'll update PR accordingly and ping infra-security for the IAM bits. Anyone want to review the PR before I mark for canary?

jen: I can review. Ping me once draft is up.

ravi: happy to review the controller lambda.

mira: I'll check TF details and the lifecycle hooks.

alex: thanks all. Will open PR in ~30m and drop link here. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: @alex infra runbook required before canary; include `runbook.md` with rollback steps.
